agents.name: Bob
memories: Water is the constraint that ends farms.
Do not plant more than we can water.

today.why: Water is the constraint that ends farms. The ripe ear is in the bin and a new row just went down under clear sky — push moisture onto the sprout before the ditch only slows the sip.
today.expect: East field near the brim so the sprout holds through another clear day.

yesterday.why: Water is the constraint that ends farms — and a ripe ear left standing is the other way we lose. Clear sky, ditch holding, cistern full from this morning's draw: take the corn while it is sure.
yesterday.expect: Corn in the bin and an empty row ready for the next seed.

agents.name: Alice
memories: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve.
Ditches compound. Heat does not wait.

today.why: Unused seeds are a delay only when the field is empty — the next row is already in. Ditches compound. Heat does not wait; timber while the sprout advances is the other compounding play.
today.expect: Wood pile thicker before the sprout asks for hands again.

yesterday.why: Unused seeds are a delay, not a reserve. After Bob clears the ripe row, put the next one down under the same ditch and clear heat — ditches compound only if something is growing in them.
yesterday.expect: A seeded row before the empty field sits a full day.
